result.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
result.summary: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but long-CoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critic-training recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 S3AC，一套面向长 CoT 推理的 actor-critic 训练方案：通过稳定 critic 训练流程缓解长轨迹覆盖不足与 value head 初期梯度主导问题，使 critic 能给出 token 级优势和 prompt 级基线，并据此设计难度感知的 prompt 采样（DAPS），在 1.5B 至 397B 的稠密与 MoE 模型上优于 GRPO 变体。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 RLVR 工作，不涉及视觉状态；但其 token 级 credit assignment 与基于难度的 rollout 选择，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹的贡献分配、监督信号粒度与计算开销取舍提供可核查的方法线索。
